title: Part 1
text: Was eating other humans ever a smart way to survive starvation? An archaeologist decided to do the math.

title: Part 2
text: Some researchers have wondered whether early humans turned to cannibalism simply because they were hungry. It sounds plausible. Survival is survival.
nxt: But in 2017, the archaeologist James Cole of the University of Brighton decided to test the idea, in the journal Scientific Reports. He asked a simple question.

nxt: How many calories are actually in a human body?

title: Part 2
text: How many calories are actually in a human body?
prev: But in 2017, the archaeologist James Cole of the University of Brighton decided to test the idea, in the journal Scientific Reports. He asked a simple question.

title: Part 3
text: His calculation used an adult man weighing about sixty-six kilograms. The whole body comes to roughly one hundred and forty-four thousand calories.
nxt: The parts people would normally eat add up to about one hundred and twenty-six thousand. That sounds like a lot.

title: Part 4
text: But look closer. The skeletal muscle, the actual meat, is only about thirty-two thousand calories. The heart offers about six hundred and fifty.
nxt: The kidneys, about three hundred and eighty. The brain and nerves, about two thousand seven hundred. Measured against the work of getting it, that is a poor return.

title: Part 5
text: Now compare it with the prey of prehistoric hunters. Cole estimated that the muscle of a mammoth holds about three point six million calories.
nxt: A woolly rhinoceros holds about one point two six million. Even a red deer holds about one hundred and sixty-four thousand, several times more than a person.

title: Part 6
text: Here is his own comparison. Imagine a group of twenty-five adults. If their only food were one human body, the muscle would last about half a day.
nxt: A mammoth could feed the same group for about two months.

title: Part 7
text: So what did Cole conclude? That the low food value points toward social or cultural explanations, not purely nutritional ones. This does not mean it never happened.
nxt: Archaeologists have found cut-marked human bones at many ancient sites. It means hunger alone is a weak explanation.

title: Part 8
text: There is one more cost. Hunting a person is far riskier than hunting a deer, because people fight back. That is common-sense inference, not a measured result.
nxt: But add the disease risk, and the picture is clear.

title: Part 9
text: The numbers say the same thing as the biology. It was a terrible deal. The full video shows how it all fits together.
